summary: Fire Atlas is an interactive wildfire-activity explorer built around NASA FIRMS MODIS and VIIRS hotspot observations. It helps users see when and where satellite instruments detected likely vegetation fires, compare the two sensors, and place current activity in historical context. The platform filters observations by confidence and fire type, aggregates them into 5 × 5 km grid-cell days, and provides a harmonized time series that bridges the MODIS-to-VIIRS sensor transition. Users can explore a calendar, hotspot maps, a 3D Earth view, seasonal history, sensor agreement, near-real-time data, and their own FIRMS CSV uploads. Fire Atlas makes satellite fire detections more interpretable for researchers, educators, communities, and decision-makers while clearly distinguishing detected activity from fire extent, incident counts, or hazard forecasts.
details:
Fire Atlas combines a FastAPI backend with a Next.js/React/TypeScript frontend. The backend processes historical, near-real-time, and user-uploaded FIRMS observations; retains MODIS detections with confidence ≥30 and VIIRS nominal/high-confidence detections; filters for likely vegetation fires where type is available; and aggregates records by UTC day and equal-area 5 km grid cell. It also calibrates VIIRS activity to a MODIS-equivalent series using quarterly overlap relationships, then evaluates that adjustment against held-out data.

The frontend presents daily activity calendars, regional hotspot maps, historical comparisons to the same-month median, raw MODIS/VIIRS/combined views, CSV export, custom geographic bounds, and an accessible Three.js globe with reduced-motion and non-WebGL fallbacks. We used Python/FastAPI, Next.js, React, TypeScript, Three.js, Playwright tests, and NASA FIRMS/GIBS imagery resources. The creative contribution is translating two different satellite records into one transparent, explorable story without implying that hotspot detections equal total burned area or risk.
